set -ex

# Defensive: /workspace is a volumeClaimTemplate PVC, not a fresh
# emptyDir. A pod reschedule/retry on this cluster's bursty
# autoscaler can re-run this step against a PVC that already has
# a partial clone from a prior attempt, and `git clone` refuses
# to write into a non-empty directory. Clear it first so the
# step is idempotent regardless of why it's re-running.
rm -rf /workspace/* /workspace/.[!.]* 2>/dev/null || true

git clone --depth 1 --branch main \
  "https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/NEEDLE.git" \
  /workspace
cd /workspace

# First cargo/rustc call in the repo — rustup installs the toolchain
rustc --version

# Warm cache via sccache->Garage when the secret is present; else cold.
if [ -n "${SCCACHE_BUCKET:-}" ] && [ -n "${SCCACHE_ENDPOINT:-}" ]; then
  # The builder image predates sccache. Bootstrap a pinned portable
  # binary until the image is rebuilt with sccache baked in.
  if ! command -v sccache >/dev/null; then
    SCCACHE_VERSION="0.17.0"
    SCCACHE_ARCHIVE="sccache-v${SCCACHE_VERSION}-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"
    SCCACHE_SHA256="67c4a96dd237c1f518f6b36083f270f9976d516f1e57fce891755ea782e50006"
    SCCACHE_TMP="/tmp/${SCCACHE_ARCHIVE}"
    SCCACHE_ROOT="/tmp/sccache-${SCCACHE_VERSION}"
    mkdir -p "$SCCACHE_ROOT"
    curl -fsSL --retry 3 \
      "https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/releases/download/v${SCCACHE_VERSION}/${SCCACHE_ARCHIVE}" \
      -o "$SCCACHE_TMP"
    echo "${SCCACHE_SHA256}  ${SCCACHE_TMP}" | sha256sum -c -
    tar -xzf "$SCCACHE_TMP" --strip-components=1 -C "$SCCACHE_ROOT"
    chmod 0755 "$SCCACHE_ROOT/sccache"
    export PATH="$SCCACHE_ROOT:$PATH"
  fi
  # Garage is exposed through the public HTTPS S3 endpoint.
  export RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache SCCACHE_S3_USE_SSL=true SCCACHE_REGION=garage
  echo "sccache enabled (bucket=$SCCACHE_BUCKET)"
  sccache --start-server 2>/dev/null || true
else
  echo "sccache NOT configured — cold build (see sccache-garage secret)"
fi

# Run the unified Definition of Done (both fast and slow lanes)
# This is the SAME command invoked by:
#   - Pre-commit hook (fast lane only)
#   - NEEDLE validation gate (fast lane only)
#   - CI verify step (both lanes, here)
#
# Lanes:
#   - Fast: fmt, clippy, check (seconds, run locally under cgroup)
#   - Slow: unit tests plus every core strand integration target
# Behavior: Aggregates all failures rather than aborting on first.
#
# CARGO_BUILD_JOBS / RUST_TEST_THREADS are set explicitly below to
# match this step's cpu limit (3000m). Without them, both rustc's
# build parallelism and libtest's default thread pool size from
# available_parallelism(), which reads the node's core count
# (compute1-8 = 4), not this container's 3-core cgroup quota.
# That oversubscription caused every needle-ci run for ~28-46h
# (2026-08-17/18) to hang past the 3600s step deadline and get
# SIGTERM'd mid-suite — confirmed by comparing three failed pods'
# logs: a *different* test was left "running for over 60 seconds"
# with no completion line in each run, which fits scheduling
# contention, not a deterministic single-test hang.
#
# The real P2/P3 strand fixtures use the pinned bead-rs CLI. Older
# builder images predate that dependency, so provision it here when
# necessary. The full commit pin matches NEEDLE's backend contract.
if ! command -v bead >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=== Installing pinned bead-rs CLI (v0.1.3) ==="
  cargo install --locked \
    --git https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/bead-rs.git \
    --rev 85f36acba864bf60f8f06b7fbe3de33c280f3d08 \
    --bin bead
fi
bead --version

echo "=== Running Definition of Done (all lanes) ==="
./scripts/definition-of-done.sh --all

# Output sccache stats if configured
command -v sccache >/dev/null && sccache --show-stats >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "sccache cache stats:" && sccache --show-stats

echo "Verify passed"

containers.name: reaper
args:
NS="${NAMESPACE}"
INTERVAL="${INTERVAL_SECONDS}"
MAX_AGE="${ERROR_AGE_SECONDS}"

log() { echo "[$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')] $*"; }

log "stale-error-workflow-reaper starting: ns=${NS} interval=${INTERVAL}s max_age=${MAX_AGE}s dry_run=${DRY_RUN}"

for verb_res in "list workflows" "delete workflows"; do
  if kubectl auth can-i ${verb_res} -n "${NS}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "permission ok: ${verb_res} in ${NS}"
  else
    log "WARNING: cannot ${verb_res} in ${NS} — RBAC not in effect yet; will keep retrying"
  fi
done

# No `set -e`: a transient API error must not kill the loop.
while true; do
  workflows_json=$(kubectl get workflows -n "${NS}" -o json 2>/tmp/reaper-wf-err)
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    log "ERROR: cannot list workflows in ${NS}: $(head -c 300 /tmp/reaper-wf-err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    log "ERROR: not reaping this pass"
    sleep "${INTERVAL}"
    continue
  fi

  # Error-phase workflows older than the retention threshold.
  # Age is computed in jq (fromdateiso8601) so the shell never
  # has to parse timestamps -- busybox `date -d` is not
  # reliable for that.
  candidates=$(echo "${workflows_json}" | jq -r --argjson max_age "${MAX_AGE}" '
    .items[]
    | select(.status.phase == "Error")
    | select(((now - (.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdateiso8601)) | floor) >= $max_age)
    | "\(.metadata.name) \(.status.message // "no message" | .[0:120])"
  ' 2>/dev/null)

  if [ -z "${candidates}" ]; then
    errors=$(echo "${workflows_json}" | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Error")] | length')
    log "no Error workflows past retention (${errors} Error-phase examined)"
  else
    echo "${candidates}" | while IFS=' ' read -r wf msg; do
      [ -z "${wf}" ] && continue
      if [ "${DRY_RUN}" = "true" ]; then
        log "DRY_RUN would delete ${wf}: ${msg}"
      else
        log "deleting ${wf}: ${msg}"
        kubectl delete workflow "${wf}" -n "${NS}" --wait=false \
          || log "delete failed for ${wf}, will retry next pass"
      fi
    done
  fi

  sleep "${INTERVAL}"
done

containers.name: reaper
args:
NS="${NAMESPACE}"
INTERVAL="${INTERVAL_SECONDS}"
GRACE="${GRACE_SECONDS}"

log() { echo "[$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')] $*"; }

log "stuck-workflow-reaper starting: ns=${NS} interval=${INTERVAL}s grace=${GRACE}s dry_run=${DRY_RUN}"

# Report the permission state at boot. Without this, an RBAC
# mismatch (wrong ServiceAccount namespace in the RoleBinding,
# say) looks identical to a healthy reaper with nothing to do.
for verb_res in "list pods" "delete workflows"; do
  if kubectl auth can-i ${verb_res} -n "${NS}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "permission ok: ${verb_res} in ${NS}"
  else
    log "WARNING: cannot ${verb_res} in ${NS} — RBAC not in effect yet; will keep retrying"
  fi
done

# No `set -e`: a transient API error must not kill the loop.
while true; do
  # Fetch first and check the exit status, rather than piping
  # straight into jq. If the API call fails — most likely RBAC
  # not yet applied — the pipeline yields an empty result, which
  # is indistinguishable from "nothing to clean up". Reporting a
  # permission failure as "all clear" is how a broken janitor
  # looks healthy indefinitely, so it must be logged loudly and
  # must not be mistaken for a successful empty pass.
  pods_json=$(kubectl get pods -n "${NS}" -o json 2>/tmp/reaper-err)
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    log "ERROR: cannot list pods in ${NS}: $(head -c 300 /tmp/reaper-err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    log "ERROR: not reaping this pass — cannot distinguish a clean cluster from a blind one"
    sleep "${INTERVAL}"
    continue
  fi

  # A workflow is a candidate when at least one of its pods is
  # wedged on an image pull AND none of its pods are Running.
  # The second condition matters: a multi-step workflow with one
  # bad step but other steps still executing is doing real work
  # and must not be reaped.
  candidates=$(echo "${pods_json}" | jq -r '
    [ .items[]
      | select(.metadata.labels["workflows.argoproj.io/workflow"] != null)
      | { wf: .metadata.labels["workflows.argoproj.io/workflow"],
          stuck: ([ (.status.containerStatuses // [])[]
                    | select(((.state.waiting // {}).reason // "")
                             | test("ImagePullBackOff|ErrImagePull")) ] | length > 0),
          live: (.status.phase == "Running") }
    ] as $p
    | ( [ $p[] | select(.stuck) | .wf ] | unique ) as $stuck
    | ( [ $p[] | select(.live)  | .wf ] | unique ) as $live
    | ( $stuck - $live ) | .[]' 2>/dev/null)

  if [ -z "${candidates}" ]; then
    # Genuinely nothing to do — the API call above succeeded, so
    # this is a real empty result rather than a blind one.
    log "no unstartable workflows ($(echo "${pods_json}" | jq -r '.items | length') pods examined)"
  else
    for wf in ${candidates}; do
      meta=$(kubectl get workflow "${wf}" -n "${NS}" -o json 2>/dev/null)
      if [ -z "${meta}" ]; then
        continue
      fi

      phase=$(echo "${meta}" | jq -r '.status.phase // "Unknown"')
      age=$(echo "${meta}" | jq -r '(now - (.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdateiso8601)) | floor')

      # Only ever touch workflows the controller still considers
      # active. Anything already terminal is ttlStrategy's job.
      if [ "${phase}" != "Running" ] && [ "${phase}" != "Pending" ]; then
        continue
      fi

      if [ "${age}" -lt "${GRACE}" ]; then
        log "skip ${wf}: image pull failing but age ${age}s < grace ${GRACE}s"
        continue
      fi

      if [ "${DRY_RUN}" = "true" ]; then
        log "DRY_RUN would delete ${wf} (phase=${phase} age=${age}s, pods cannot pull image)"
      else
        log "deleting ${wf} (phase=${phase} age=${age}s, pods cannot pull image)"
        kubectl delete workflow "${wf}" -n "${NS}" --wait=false \
          || log "delete failed for ${wf}, will retry next pass"
      fi
    done
  fi

  sleep "${INTERVAL}"
done

containers.name: reaper
args:
NS="${NAMESPACE}"
INTERVAL="${INTERVAL_SECONDS}"
GRACE="${GRACE_SECONDS}"

log() { echo "[$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')] $*"; }

log "superseded-workflow-reaper starting: ns=${NS} interval=${INTERVAL}s grace=${GRACE}s dry_run=${DRY_RUN}"

for verb_res in "list pods" "list workflows" "delete workflows"; do
  if kubectl auth can-i ${verb_res} -n "${NS}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log "permission ok: ${verb_res} in ${NS}"
  else
    log "WARNING: cannot ${verb_res} in ${NS} — RBAC not in effect yet; will keep retrying"
  fi
done

# No `set -e`: a transient API error must not kill the loop.
while true; do
  workflows_json=$(kubectl get workflows -n "${NS}" -o json 2>/tmp/reaper-wf-err)
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    log "ERROR: cannot list workflows in ${NS}: $(head -c 300 /tmp/reaper-wf-err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    log "ERROR: not reaping this pass"
    sleep "${INTERVAL}"
    continue
  fi

  pods_json=$(kubectl get pods -n "${NS}" -o json 2>/tmp/reaper-pod-err)
  if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    log "ERROR: cannot list pods in ${NS}: $(head -c 300 /tmp/reaper-pod-err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    log "ERROR: not reaping this pass — cannot tell which workflows have started"
    sleep "${INTERVAL}"
    continue
  fi

  # Workflows with at least one pod that has left Pending: they
  # got scheduled and are (or were) actually running. Never
  # reap these, no matter their sync-queue position.
  started_wfs=$(echo "${pods_json}" | jq -r '
    [ .items[]
      | select(.metadata.labels["workflows.argoproj.io/workflow"] != null)
      | select(.status.phase != "Pending")
      | .metadata.labels["workflows.argoproj.io/workflow"]
    ] | unique | .[]' 2>/dev/null)

  # Within each WorkflowTemplate's still-active (Pending or
  # Running) workflows, keep only the newest; everything else
  # in that group is a candidate. age is computed in jq
  # (fromdateiso8601) so the shell never has to parse
  # timestamps — busybox `date -d` is not reliable for that.
  candidates=$(echo "${workflows_json}" | jq -r '
    [ .items[]
      | select(.status.phase == "Pending" or .status.phase == "Running")
      | select(.spec.workflowTemplateRef.name != null)
      | { name: .metadata.name,
          template: .spec.workflowTemplateRef.name,
          created: .metadata.creationTimestamp,
          age: ((now - (.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdateiso8601)) | floor) }
    ]
    | group_by(.template)
    | map(select(length > 1))
    | map(sort_by(.created) | reverse)
    | .[]
    | .[1:][]
    | "\(.name) \(.template) \(.age)"
  ' 2>/dev/null)

  if [ -z "${candidates}" ]; then
    active=$(echo "${workflows_json}" | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Pending" or .status.phase=="Running")] | length')
    log "no superseded workflows (${active} active examined)"
  else
    echo "${candidates}" | while IFS=' ' read -r wf template age; do
      [ -z "${wf}" ] && continue

      if echo "${started_wfs}" | grep -qx "${wf}"; then
        log "skip ${wf} (template=${template}): superseded but already started — letting it finish"
        continue
      fi

      if [ "${age}" -lt "${GRACE}" ]; then
        log "skip ${wf} (template=${template}): superseded but age ${age}s < grace ${GRACE}s"
        continue
      fi

      if [ "${DRY_RUN}" = "true" ]; then
        log "DRY_RUN would delete ${wf} (template=${template}, age=${age}s, never started, superseded by a newer push)"
      else
        log "deleting ${wf} (template=${template}, age=${age}s, never started, superseded by a newer push)"
        kubectl delete workflow "${wf}" -n "${NS}" --wait=false \
          || log "delete failed for ${wf}, will retry next pass"
      fi
    done
  fi

  sleep "${INTERVAL}"
done

containers.name: backup
args:
# NOT `set -e`: this is a long-lived loop and a single failed repo
# must not kill the container. Failures are counted and reported.
set -u

apk add --no-cache postgresql-client git curl jq aws-cli >/dev/null

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$ARMOR_ACCESS_KEY"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$ARMOR_SECRET_KEY"
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="us-east-1"
# MULTIPART IS ENABLED. The previous note here said ARMOR rejected
# multipart (InvalidPartOrder on concurrent uploads, InvalidPartSize
# on a non-aligned trailing part) and disabled it by setting the
# threshold to 5GB — making every object a single PUT.
#
# That note is stale, and it was the direct cause of a real backup
# failure: ARMOR sustains only ~4 MB/s (measured: 50MB in 13s, 200MB
# in 49s), so unfairmarket-research (1.5GB) needed a ~6.5 minute
# single PUT and aide-de-camp (2.2GB) ~9 minutes. One blip anywhere
# in that window discards the entire transfer, and on 2026-08-08
# unfairmarket-research ended up with NO backup at all.
#
# Re-tested against live ARMOR 2026-08-08, both cases the old note
# warned about:
#   - sequential (max_concurrent_requests=1) + 64MiB chunks: WORKS
#   - trailing part deliberately NOT 65536-aligned (157,298,745
#     bytes): WORKS, remote ContentLength matched byte-exact
# So ARMOR has been fixed since that note was written. Multipart
# means a transient failure costs one 64MiB part, not 1.5GB.
#
# Keep max_concurrent_requests=1: sequential ordering is what
# avoided InvalidPartOrder, and it is still the safe assumption.
# 64MiB = 1024 x 65536, block-aligned by construction.
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 1
aws configure set default.s3.multipart_threshold 64MB
aws configure set default.s3.multipart_chunksize 64MB
# ARMOR is slow enough that a large part can outlast the default
# 60s read timeout; give it room rather than failing a whole repo.
aws configure set default.cli_read_timeout 900
aws configure set default.cli_connect_timeout 60

ARMOR="http://armor.armor.svc.cluster.local:9000"
FORGEJO="http://forgejo-gitea-http.forgejo.svc.cluster.local:3000"
FORGEJO_HOST="forgejo-gitea-http.forgejo.svc.cluster.local"
BUCKET="iad-ci"

# ── Credentials: a PAT, never the admin password ─────────────
# The admin password was rotated inside Forgejo on ~2026-08-09
# without the change reaching the Secret or OpenBao, and the
# backup died at enumeration for 20 consecutive runs (~42h, zero
# repos). A token survives password rotation and needs no admin
# rights, since this job only reads.
#
# Kept out of the process list for the original reason too:
# It was previously embedded in the git clone URL and passed to
# curl via -u, so `ps` inside this pod showed the plaintext
# credential to every process — and to anyone running
# `kubectl exec`. GIT_ASKPASS and a netrc file pass it through
# the environment and a 0600 file instead of argv.
umask 077
printf '#!/bin/sh\nprintf "%%s" "$BACKUP_TOKEN"\n' > /tmp/askpass.sh
chmod 700 /tmp/askpass.sh
export GIT_ASKPASS=/tmp/askpass.sh
export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
printf 'machine %s login %s password %s\n' \
  "$FORGEJO_HOST" "$ADMIN_USER" "$BACKUP_TOKEN" > /tmp/netrc
chmod 600 /tmp/netrc
HEALTH=/tmp/healthy
RETAIN="${RETAIN_COPIES:-7}"
PACE="${PACE_SECONDS:-2}"
VERIFY_EVERY="${VERIFY_EVERY_RUNS:-7}"

# ── Queue-based retry ────────────────────────────────────────
# Repos are a WORK QUEUE, not a linear pass. Anything that fails
# is re-queued and retried in a later sweep, with a long wait in
# between.
#
# Why: on 2026-08-08 a run lost 7 repos to
# "Could not resolve host: forgejo-gitea-http...", and they were a
# CONTIGUOUS alphabetical block (gantry-rs..mobile-gaming, with
# mta-my-way succeeding straight after). That is one cluster-DNS
# blip lasting minutes, not seven independent repo problems. The
# then-current retry was 3 attempts with sleep 5s/10s — a ~15
# second budget, i.e. the same request three times inside one
# outage. The verification phase had no retry at all, which is
# why 10 repos afterwards reported NO BACKUP for data that was
# present.
#
# The queue is the right shape because the failure mode is
# correlated and time-bounded: by the time a later sweep runs,
# the blip is over. Inline attempts stay small (they only cover
# momentary errors); the sweeps do the real work.
MAX_SWEEPS="${MAX_SWEEPS:-4}"
INLINE_ATTEMPTS="${INLINE_ATTEMPTS:-2}"

# Wait before sweep N+1. Escalates well past a typical control
# plane blip. A sweep in which NOTHING succeeded is treated as a
# full outage and always takes the longest wait.
sweep_backoff() {
  case "$1" in
    1) echo 60 ;;
    2) echo 300 ;;
    *) echo 900 ;;
  esac
}
run=0

s3() { aws "$@" --endpoint-url "$ARMOR"; }

while true; do
  run=$((run + 1))
  STAMP=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M)
  echo "=== Backup start: $(date -u) (run $run) ==="
  rm -f "$HEALTH"
  fail=0

  # ── PostgreSQL ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  echo "--- postgres dump ---"
  if PGPASSWORD="$DB_PASS" pg_dump \
       -h forgejo-postgres-rw.forgejo.svc.cluster.local \
       -U forgejo forgejo | gzip | \
       s3 s3 cp - "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/postgres/$STAMP.sql.gz"; then
    echo "postgres: ok"
  else
    echo "postgres: FAILED"; fail=$((fail + 1))
  fi

  # ── Enumerate every repo the server knows about ───────────────
  # Written to a file, not piped, so the loop below is NOT a
  # subshell and its counters survive.
  : > /tmp/live.txt
  page=1
  api_ok=1
  while true; do
    body=$(curl -sf -H "Authorization: token $BACKUP_TOKEN" \
      "$FORGEJO/api/v1/repos/search?limit=50&page=$page") || { api_ok=0; break; }
    names=$(echo "$body" | jq -r '.data[].full_name')
    [ -z "$names" ] && break
    echo "$names" >> /tmp/live.txt
    page=$((page + 1))
  done
  TOTAL=$(wc -l < /tmp/live.txt | tr -d ' ')
  if [ "$api_ok" -eq 0 ] || [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: could not enumerate repos — refusing to report success"
    echo "=== Backup INCOMPLETE: $(date -u) ==="
    sleep 3600     # retry in an hour rather than waiting a full day
    continue
  fi
  echo "--- repo backup ($TOTAL repos) ---"

  ok=0
  mkdir -p /tmp/repos
  cp /tmp/live.txt /tmp/queue.txt
  sweep=1
  while [ -s /tmp/queue.txt ] && [ "$sweep" -le "$MAX_SWEEPS" ]; do
   : > /tmp/retry.txt
   sweep_ok=0
   queued=$(wc -l < /tmp/queue.txt | tr -d ' ')
   [ "$sweep" -gt 1 ] && echo "--- sweep $sweep: retrying $queued repo(s) ---"
   while IFS= read -r repo; do
    [ -n "$repo" ] || continue
    owner=${repo%%/*}
    name=${repo#*/}
    d="/tmp/repos/$name.git"
    t="/tmp/$name.tar.gz"
    rm -rf "$d" "$t"

    # Retry: the failure mode being fixed was transient
    # unreachability, where 47 repos failed in ~16 seconds. One
    # blip should not cost a day of backups for every repo after it.
    cloned=0
    n=1
    while [ "$n" -le "$INLINE_ATTEMPTS" ]; do
      # stderr is captured to a file and echoed on failure —
      # discarding it is why the previous outage was
      # undiagnosable. NOT piped into sed: in a pipeline the exit
      # status is sed's, so `if git ... | sed` would report
      # success for every failed clone.
      # Username only in the URL; the password comes from
      # GIT_ASKPASS so it never appears in argv.
      if git clone --quiet --mirror \
           "http://$ADMIN_USER@$FORGEJO_HOST:3000/$repo.git" \
           "$d" >/tmp/clone.err 2>&1; then
        cloned=1; break
      fi
      echo "  $repo: clone attempt $n failed:"
      sed 's/^/      /' /tmp/clone.err | head -5
      rm -rf "$d"; sleep $((n * 5)); n=$((n + 1))
    done
    if [ "$cloned" -ne 1 ]; then
      echo "repo $repo: clone failed, re-queued"; echo "$repo" >> /tmp/retry.txt; continue
    fi

    head_sha=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    tar czf "$t" -C /tmp/repos "$name.git" 2>/dev/null

    # Verify the artifact before trusting it. Catches truncation
    # and corruption at write time rather than at restore time.
    if ! tar tzf "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "repo $repo: tarball corrupt, re-queued"
      echo "$repo" >> /tmp/retry.txt; rm -rf "$d" "$t"; continue
    fi
    local_size=$(wc -c < "$t" | tr -d ' ')

    # Date-stamped key. A failed run can no longer masquerade as a
    # good one by leaving an old object in place.
    key="forgejo/repos/$owner/$name/$STAMP.tar.gz"
    # Uploads are retried for the same reason clones are: ARMOR
    # read timeouts are transient and cost a whole repo's backup
    # otherwise. Observed 2026-08-08 — one repo failed upload and
    # was left with NO backup at all, because the date-stamped key
    # means there is no previous object to fall back on.
    uploaded=0
    u=1
    while [ "$u" -le "$INLINE_ATTEMPTS" ]; do
      if s3 s3 cp "$t" "s3://$BUCKET/$key" >/tmp/upload.err 2>&1; then
        uploaded=1; break
      fi
      echo "  $repo: upload attempt $u failed:"
      sed 's/^/      /' /tmp/upload.err | head -3
      sleep $((u * 10)); u=$((u + 1))
    done
    if [ "$uploaded" -ne 1 ]; then
      echo "repo $repo: upload failed, re-queued"; echo "$repo" >> /tmp/retry.txt; rm -rf "$d" "$t"; continue
    fi

    # Confirm what landed matches what was sent.
    remote_size=$(s3 s3api head-object --bucket "$BUCKET" --key "$key" \
                    --query ContentLength --output text 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "$remote_size" != "$local_size" ]; then
      echo "repo $repo: size mismatch local=$local_size remote=$remote_size, re-queued"
      echo "$repo" >> /tmp/retry.txt; rm -rf "$d" "$t"; continue
    fi

    echo "repo $repo: ok head=${head_sha:-none} bytes=$local_size"
    ok=$((ok + 1)); sweep_ok=$((sweep_ok + 1))

    # Retention: keep the newest $RETAIN copies of this repo.
    # busybox `head` has no negative -n, so the drop count is
    # computed explicitly rather than using `head -n -N`.
    s3 s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/repos/$owner/$name/" 2>/dev/null \
      | awk '{print $4}' | sort > /tmp/copies.txt
    ncopies=$(wc -l < /tmp/copies.txt | tr -d ' ')
    if [ "$ncopies" -gt "$RETAIN" ]; then
      head -n $((ncopies - RETAIN)) /tmp/copies.txt | while IFS= read -r old; do
        [ -n "$old" ] && s3 s3 rm "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/repos/$owner/$name/$old" >/dev/null 2>&1
      done
    fi

    rm -rf "$d" "$t"
    sleep "$PACE"   # don't hammer Forgejo; it serves the fleet
   done < /tmp/queue.txt

   mv /tmp/retry.txt /tmp/queue.txt
   left=$(wc -l < /tmp/queue.txt | tr -d ' ')
   if [ "$left" -gt 0 ] && [ "$sweep" -lt "$MAX_SWEEPS" ]; then
     # A sweep in which nothing at all succeeded is a full outage,
     # not bad luck on individual repos — wait the long interval
     # regardless of which sweep number this is.
     if [ "$sweep_ok" -eq 0 ]; then
       w=$(sweep_backoff 99)
       echo "sweep $sweep: 0/$queued succeeded — treating as an outage, waiting ${w}s"
     else
       w=$(sweep_backoff "$sweep")
       echo "sweep $sweep: $left repo(s) failed, waiting ${w}s before retrying"
     fi
     sleep "$w"
   fi
   sweep=$((sweep + 1))
  done
  # Whatever is still queued after every sweep is a real failure.
  fail=$((fail + $(wc -l < /tmp/queue.txt | tr -d ' ')))
  if [ -s /tmp/queue.txt ]; then
    echo "unrecovered after $MAX_SWEEPS sweeps:"
    sed 's/^/    /' /tmp/queue.txt
  fi
  rm -rf /tmp/repos

  # ── Periodic restore test ─────────────────────────────────────
  # Proves the artifacts are actually restorable, not merely present.
  if [ $((run % VERIFY_EVERY)) -eq 1 ]; then
    # Same queue treatment as the backup phase. Previously this
    # had no retry at all, so one blip during verification
    # reported NO BACKUP for 10 repos whose data was present —
    # a false alarm on the exact signal the probe gates on.
    echo "--- restore verification ---"
    vok=0
    cp /tmp/live.txt /tmp/vqueue.txt
    vsweep=1
    while [ -s /tmp/vqueue.txt ] && [ "$vsweep" -le "$MAX_SWEEPS" ]; do
     : > /tmp/vretry.txt
     vsweep_ok=0
     vqueued=$(wc -l < /tmp/vqueue.txt | tr -d ' ')
     [ "$vsweep" -gt 1 ] && echo "--- verify sweep $vsweep: retrying $vqueued repo(s) ---"
     while IFS= read -r repo; do
      [ -n "$repo" ] || continue
      owner=${repo%%/*}; name=${repo#*/}
      latest=$(s3 s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/repos/$owner/$name/" 2>/dev/null \
                 | awk '{print $4}' | sort | tail -1)
      # NO BACKUP is now re-queued too: an empty listing is far
      # more often a transient ARMOR/network failure than a
      # genuinely absent object.
      [ -z "$latest" ] && { echo "verify $repo: no object listed, re-queued"; echo "$repo" >> /tmp/vretry.txt; continue; }
      rm -rf /tmp/vx; mkdir -p /tmp/vx
      if s3 s3 cp "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/repos/$owner/$name/$latest" /tmp/vx/a.tar.gz >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && tar xzf /tmp/vx/a.tar.gz -C /tmp/vx 2>/dev/null \
         && git -C "/tmp/vx/$name.git" rev-parse HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && git -C "/tmp/vx/$name.git" fsck --connectivity-only --no-progress >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        vok=$((vok+1)); vsweep_ok=$((vsweep_ok+1))
      else
        echo "verify $repo: restore failed ($latest), re-queued"; echo "$repo" >> /tmp/vretry.txt
      fi
      rm -rf /tmp/vx
     done < /tmp/vqueue.txt

     mv /tmp/vretry.txt /tmp/vqueue.txt
     vleft=$(wc -l < /tmp/vqueue.txt | tr -d ' ')
     if [ "$vleft" -gt 0 ] && [ "$vsweep" -lt "$MAX_SWEEPS" ]; then
       if [ "$vsweep_ok" -eq 0 ]; then
         w=$(sweep_backoff 99)
         echo "verify sweep $vsweep: 0/$vqueued succeeded — treating as an outage, waiting ${w}s"
       else
         w=$(sweep_backoff "$vsweep")
         echo "verify sweep $vsweep: $vleft repo(s) failed, waiting ${w}s"
       fi
       sleep "$w"
     fi
     vsweep=$((vsweep + 1))
    done
    vfail=$(wc -l < /tmp/vqueue.txt | tr -d ' ')
    echo "verification: restorable=$vok failed=$vfail"
    if [ "$vfail" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "unverified after $MAX_SWEEPS sweeps:"; sed 's/^/    /' /tmp/vqueue.txt
      fail=$((fail + vfail))
    fi
  fi

  # ── Coverage accounting and health ───────────────────────────
  echo "coverage: $ok/$TOTAL repos backed up, $fail failure(s)"
  if [ "$ok" -eq "$TOTAL" ] && [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then complete=true; else complete=false; fi
  # printf, not a heredoc: a heredoc terminator must sit at column
  # zero, and everything here is indented inside a YAML block
  # scalar, so `<<JSON ... JSON` would never terminate.
  printf '{"stamp":"%s","total_repos":%s,"backed_up":%s,"failures":%s,"complete":%s}\n' \
    "$STAMP" "$TOTAL" "$ok" "$fail" "$complete" \
    | s3 s3 cp - "s3://$BUCKET/forgejo/status/latest.json" >/dev/null 2>&1

  if [ "$complete" = "true" ]; then
    touch "$HEALTH"
    echo "=== Backup COMPLETE: $(date -u) — $ok/$TOTAL ==="
  else
    # No health file → readiness probe fails → NotReady in
    # `kubectl get pods` and Degraded in ArgoCD. This is the alert.
    echo "=== Backup INCOMPLETE: $(date -u) — $ok/$TOTAL, $fail failure(s) ==="
  fi

  sleep 86400
done

containers.name: init
args:
set -e
apk add --no-cache curl

FORGEJO="http://forgejo-gitea-http.forgejo.svc.cluster.local:3000"
umask 077
netrc_escape() {
  sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'
}
NETRC_USER=$(printf '%s' "$ADMIN_USER" | netrc_escape)
NETRC_PASS=$(printf '%s' "$ADMIN_PASS" | netrc_escape)
printf 'machine forgejo-gitea-http.forgejo.svc.cluster.local\nlogin "%s"\npassword "%s"\n' \
  "$NETRC_USER" "$NETRC_PASS" > /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc
unset NETRC_USER NETRC_PASS

until curl -sf "$FORGEJO/api/healthz" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  echo "Waiting for Forgejo API..."
  sleep 10
done
echo "Forgejo is up"

CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
  --netrc \
  --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
  "$FORGEJO/api/v1/users/$JEDARDEN_USER")

if [ "$CODE" = "401" ] || [ "$CODE" = "403" ]; then
  echo "Forgejo password authentication is unavailable; skipping API provisioning"
  exec sleep infinity
fi

if [ "$CODE" = "200" ]; then
  echo "User $JEDARDEN_USER already exists, skipping"
else
  echo "Creating user $JEDARDEN_USER..."
  curl -sf -X POST \
    --netrc \
    --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    "$FORGEJO/api/v1/admin/users" \
    -d "{
      \"login_name\": \"$JEDARDEN_USER\",
      \"username\": \"$JEDARDEN_USER\",
      \"email\": \"$JEDARDEN_EMAIL\",
      \"password\": \"$JEDARDEN_PASS\",
      \"must_change_password\": false,
      \"send_notify\": false,
      \"source_id\": 0
    }"
  echo "User $JEDARDEN_USER created"
fi

# Push mirrors — idempotent: checks before creating
ensure_mirror() {
  local repo="$1" github_repo="$2"
  existing=$(curl -sf \
    --netrc \
    --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
    "$FORGEJO/api/v1/repos/$repo/push_mirrors" | \
    grep -c "github.com" || true)
  if [ "$existing" = "0" ]; then
    echo "Adding GitHub mirror for $repo..."
    curl -sf -X POST \
      --netrc \
      --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      "$FORGEJO/api/v1/repos/$repo/push_mirrors" \
      -d "{
        \"remote_name\": \"github\",
        \"remote_address\": \"https://github.com/${github_repo}.git\",
        \"remote_username\": \"jedarden\",
        \"remote_password\": \"$MIRROR_TOKEN\",
        \"interval\": \"10m\",
        \"sync_on_commit\": true
      }" && echo "Mirror added for $repo" || echo "Mirror add failed for $repo"
  else
    echo "Mirror already configured for $repo, skipping"
  fi
}

ensure_mirror jedarden/aivc       jedarden/aivc
ensure_mirror jedarden/brand-kit  jedarden/brand-kit
ensure_mirror jedarden/pdftract   jedarden/pdftract
ensure_mirror jedarden/zai-proxy  jedarden/zai-proxy

# Repository webhooks — idempotent desired state for Argo Events.
ensure_webhook() {
  local repo="$1" target="$2"
  existing=$(curl -sf \
    --netrc \
    --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
    "$FORGEJO/api/v1/repos/$repo/hooks" | \
    grep -F -c "\"url\":\"$target\"" || true)
  if [ "$existing" = "0" ]; then
    echo "Adding push webhook for $repo..."
    curl -sf -X POST \
      --netrc \
      --netrc-file /tmp/forgejo-admin.netrc \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      "$FORGEJO/api/v1/repos/$repo/hooks" \
      -d "{
        \"type\": \"forgejo\",
        \"active\": true,
        \"events\": [\"push\"],
        \"config\": {
          \"url\": \"$target\",
          \"content_type\": \"json\"
        }
      }" >/dev/null
    echo "Webhook added for $repo"
  else
    echo "Webhook already configured for $repo, skipping"
  fi
}

ensure_webhook jedarden/tradegraph https://webhooks-ci.ardenone.com/tradegraph

echo "Init complete"
exec sleep infinity
